item.text: {"version":"qubo-template-v1","sense":"min","decode":{"index":"i","complement":false},"terms":[{"over":"vertices","coefficient":"2**n-2**(n-1-i)","factors":[{"index":"i","complement":false}]},{"over":"edges","coefficient":"2**n","factors":[{"index":"i","complement":true},{"index":"j","complement":true}]}],"explanation":"Decode x_i=y[i]. The energy is E(x)=sum_i (2^n-2^(n-1-i))x_i + 2^n sum_{(i,j) in edges}(1-x_i)(1-x_j). Each edge term penalizes exactly an uncovered edge. If an assignment has an uncovered edge (i,j), selecting either endpoint removes at least one penalty of 2^n, creates no uncovered edges, and adds a vertex coefficient strictly less than 2^n. Thus energy strictly decreases, so every global optimum is a vertex cover. For a cover S, all penalties vanish and E(S)=2^n|S|-sum_{i in S}2^(n-1-i). The weighted sum lies between 0 and 2^n-1, so every cover with one more selected vertex has strictly greater energy than every cover with one fewer selected vertex; minimum cardinality therefore has absolute priority. Among covers of equal cardinality, minimizing E maximizes the binary-weighted incidence sum. At the smallest index where two distinct equal-cardinality selections differ, the set containing that index has the larger weighted sum and its ascending tuple is lexicographically smaller. Since the powers of two uniquely encode every selection, the canonical minimum cover is the unique optimum. When n=0, both expanded scopes are empty, the sole decoded selection is empty, and its energy is zero."}
